title: test(auth): pin that identity re-resolves across an organization switch (#5719)
body:
Part of #5719.

**This PR changes no production behaviour.** #5719 was filed as an observation whose author
could not answer the question the whole defect turns on. That question is now answered — the
answer is "no defect" — and this PR lands the pin that keeps it answered.

## The measurement

#5719's reasoning was correct as far as it went. `AuthProvider.switchOrganization` really
does not call `loadSession()` (verified at `AuthProvider.tsx:716` on `3ece13e33`), and
framework `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` really does derive
`user.positions[]` inside `customSession` from `session.activeOrganizationId`
(`if (!orgId) return []`). `useWorkspaceAdminStatus` is `leg1 || leg2 || leg3` and
short-circuits `isResolved` to `true` on any positive leg, so a stale `org_owner` would read
as a **confirmed** admin in the new organization — the over-permissive direction.

The open question was whether the server re-issues a bearer on `POST /organization/set-active`.
It does. Measured by driving better-auth **1.6.28** standalone — the version `packages/auth`
resolves — with the `organization` and `bearer` plugins the framework always enables
(`auth-manager.ts:2261`, `bearer()` with no options):

| call | `set-auth-token` | body `session.token` |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /get-session` | absent | `lu9xN8EBsuqDOlePpKblcCxnkMSgz7CO` (unsigned) |
| `POST /organization/set-active` | **present** | — |

and the value on that header was `lu9xN8EBsuqDOlePpKblcCxnkMSgz7CO.bvWj0cFhrtUI77i7tjyNuEyta+2grAAAWGaeYeB/7eY=`.

So the objectui#4467 rotation subscription already re-resolves identity across an org switch,
and `user.positions` is **not** stale. The post-switch `get-session` confirmed
`activeOrganizationId` had moved to the new organization.

## The mechanism is a spelling accident, which is why this is pinned

The switch does **not** mint a new session — `internalAdapter.updateSession` writes only
`activeOrganizationId`, and the route reaches `setSessionCookie(ctx, ...)` on its success path
(`plugins/organization/routes/crud-org.mjs`). `bearer()`'s after-hook emits `set-auth-token`
for any response that stages a session `Set-Cookie` (`plugins/bearer/index.mjs`), and the
value it emits is the **signed** `token.signature` spelling. Meanwhile
`createAuthClient.getSession()` stores `payload.session.token` — the **unsigned** value, which
is what `sys_session.token` holds. Two spellings of one session, and `TokenStorage.set`
notifies on a value change.

That is the entire guarantee, and nothing declares it. Normalising either lane onto a single
spelling — a reasonable-looking tidy-up — would silently stop identity re-resolving across an
org switch, reintroducing exactly the over-permissive gating #5719 described, with no test
anywhere to catch it.

The framework independently records the same asymmetry at `auth-manager.ts:4418`:
"`session.token` stores the UNSIGNED value ... `bearer()` hands clients the SIGNED
`token.signature` in `set-auth-token` (and accepts both back)".

## What lands

`packages/auth/src/__tests__/switchOrgIdentityReresolve-5719.test.tsx`, six cases:

1. an owner of A who is an ordinary member of B stops reading as admin after the switch;
2. **the control** — an owner of *both* still reads as admin after the switch, so case 1 cannot
   pass on code that merely stopped reporting admin;
3. exactly **one** extra session read per switch;
4. the counterfactual — a switch response echoing the token already held does **not**
   re-resolve, which is the #5719 defect shape, reachable only if the two spellings converge;
5. `getSession()` leaves the unsigned `session.token` stored even when the response rotates,
   driven through the **real** `createAuthClient`;
6. the two spellings are different strings, so one replacing the other is a rotation.

**No explicit `refreshSession()` was added.** The rotation path already spends exactly one
`get-session` per switch, so an explicit call would make every org switch cost two — a
regression on the common path traded for an edge case. The card's own caveat (that
`refreshSession` deliberately does not raise `isLoading`, so the console must not blank during
a switch) is honoured for free by not adding one.

## Ablations — both directions confirmed on disk, restored under `trap`

- **Sever the objectui#4467 rotation subscription** in `AuthProvider.tsx` → cases 1 and 3 fail,
  4 pass. Survivors are correct and localised: case 2 cannot discriminate the mechanism by
  design (both orgs answer `org_owner` either way, which is exactly what makes it the control),
  case 4 already asserts no re-resolution, and cases 5-6 never touch `AuthProvider`.
- **Remove the unsigned-token write** in `createAuthClient.getSession()` → case 5 fails with
  `expected 'sess_5719_raw.bvWj0c...' to be 'sess_5719_raw'` — storage left holding the signed
  form, which is the thesis stated as a failure.

Each mutation was confirmed by anchored occurrence counts in both directions (injected marker
0 to 1, removed anchor 1 to 0) before any result was read, and each restore verified
byte-identical by matching `git hash-object` against the committed blob.

## Verification — union run at `1d3bef350`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/auth/` — **23 files, 236 tests passed**
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/auth type-check` — green (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, script name echoed)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/auth lint` — exit 0 (the two `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`
  warnings are pre-existing in `AuthProvider.tsx`, which this PR leaves byte-untouched; the new
  file lints 0 errors / 0 warnings)
- `check-control-bytes` (4799 files), `check-package-self-import`, `check-phantom-dependencies`,
  `check-changeset-presence` (accepts the empty-frontmatter declaration explicitly),
  `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed` — all exit 0

Changeset is empty-frontmatter: tests only, this publishes nothing.
